name: Ishbak
overview: Ishbak is a male figure in the Bible identified as a son of Abraham through his wife Keturah. Beyond this unique attribute, Scripture does not provide additional details about his tribe or other distinguishing notes. His mention is brief and primarily genealogical in nature.
namesAndTitles: The name Ishbak appears as a proper name in Genesis 25:2. No specific meaning or divine origin of the name is recorded, so it is recognized simply as the personal name given to this individual.
familyAndRelationships: Ishbak is recorded as a son of Abraham and Keturah, establishing his place within Abraham's extended family. Scripture does not provide further information about his descendants or other familial connections beyond this parentage.
scriptureSignificance: Ishbak's significance lies in his role as one of the sons Abraham had with Keturah after the death of Sarah. This highlights God's provision for Abraham's lineage beyond Isaac, underscoring the faithfulness of God's promises to Abraham's family. Though not central to the biblical narrative, Ishbak represents part of the fulfillment of God's covenantal blessings through Abraham's offspring.
